subject: treasureHoard
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: treasure hoard: coins, gems, chest, crown, goblets.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
I'm planning a treasure-themed static model built efficiently with merged geometry per color: a chest with lid, bands, and lock, a mounded pile of coins, gems with glow effects, a crown with spikes, and goblets, keeping everything lightweight without needing joints.

Now I'm figuring out the layout specifics — sizing the chest body and lid, positioning the hinge for an open lid, and scattering coins in a randomized mound pattern around the chest base, all using League-of-Legends-style gilded, stylized paint textures.

Computing the arch outline points for the lid, then working out the hinge rotation math to transform local coordinates into world space as the lid swings open by roughly 105 degrees.

I'll add gold bands as scaled-up extrusions on the lid for protruding trim, build the wooden body with painted grain, gold corner trim, and a lock plate with a gem, then position the chest itself slightly back in z. For the coin mound, I'll define a height falloff function to scatter coins around the front of the chest and inside the open lid area.

Now I'm shaping the gold mound as a low-poly cone base with scattered coins on top, tilted randomly, plus a smaller mound inside the chest. I'm adding flat icosahedron gems in red, blue, green, and violet with emissive glow, scattered across the mound for sparkle.

For the crown, I'm lathing a band with five cone spikes topped by gem spheres, tilted and placed on the right side of the mound. For the goblets, I'm lathing stem-and-bowl profiles for an upright goblet resting on the mound and a fallen one nearby, gilded gold with gem-studded rims, calculating the mound's height function to position them correctly. I'm also considering adding a glowing blue crystal standing behind the chest for extra flair.

I'll skip the sack idea but add a decal emblem on the chest's front face using a texture plane, along with wood paint and gem facet textures. Writing coin geometry...

Working out the mound shape now: positioning the cone roughly centered near the chest's front so it overlaps slightly, with radius 0.8 and a height falloff function so coins sit flat near the peak and taper down toward the edges, placed just above the surface.

I'll filter out coins that intersect the chest wall itself, then handle gems using the same height-sampling approach before writing the final code.
